I can't stand RPGs. I don't enjoy the lore, I don't want to learn everything about the game world, and I couldn't care less about finding the Penis Sword Of Uberness with +2 attack damage. I didn't even like Skyrim. I have no interest in fighting stupid dragons that become progressively bigger and more ridiculous, or taking over a castle by fighting guards a few at a time.

But, I love Witcher 3, it's among my top 5 games of all time. Portal and Portal 2 probably top that list. It is so good that it overcomes its genre.

The only flaws I can think of is that it involves about 2% more travel time than is really needed (though it's a breeze compared to all other RPGs), and it doesn't separate the story arc into distinct chapters quite as well as it could. I'd like for it to have Act 1, Act 2, etc laid out somewhere. It would be nice to know that the game world updates and understands that the stuff from the prior acts is in the past. This is never actually a problem in this game because it is so well designed, but it was one of the problems that turned me away from RPGs years ago, so it's something I like to see. There is one website with a walkthrough that claims to do this, but they crammed like 5 chapters into Act 1 when they really shouldn't have.

Also, the horse is a bit dumb. He doesn't follow orders quite as quickly as he should, and it would be cool if it automatically dodged trees for you.

Those are the only problems I can find. A less-than-perfect AI, and it lacks a feature that it doesn't need anyway.

It can be resource intensive, but my machine can handle it well enough at 1440p.
